body: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":57452,"items":[{"abstract":"<jats:p>Retrieval-augmented generation serves as a novel framework that enhances factual correctness and contextual appropriateness of large language model outputs through its integration of document retrieval systems that access modern and updated external content. In this paper, a RAG pipeline that utilizes Lang Chain and Chroma DB alongside the Falcon-7B-Instruct model from Hugging Face as its core components is developed. Building on this pipeline, a novel SPE-RAG framework is proposed, which introduces a Hybrid Retrieval Scoring mechanism to address the limitations of the conventional RAG systems that rely on fixed Top-k retrieval and cosine similarity. The proposed framework combines semantic similarity, keyword relevance, document freshness, and source reliability. An Adaptive Context Selection Algorithm dynamically determines the number of retrieved document chunks. Furthermore, an Evidence Verification Layer filters unreliable passages before answer generation, and a Confidence-Aware Generation module estimates answer reliability and withholds unsupported responses when evidence is insufficient. The RAG pipeline processes input docs in chunking with overlaps, then encodes the chunks to dense vectors using a transformer-based embedding model and ingests the vectors into a vector store of ChromaDB. For inference, a semantic retriever retrieves the most related doc chunks, and a structural prompt template supplements the user\u2019s queries with the retrieved evidence to be sent to LLM. Experimental assessment is planned by employing precision, recall, and hallucination rate as evaluation metrics. Preliminary experiments suggest the efficacy of the proposed SPE-RAG framework in optimizing retriever output, reducing factual errata, and improving response faithfulness over standard RAG models.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.7519288","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["A Semantic, Probabilistic, and Evidence-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Document-Based Question Answering"],"author":[{"given":"Gudipati  Rajesh","family":"Naidu","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"ILA","family":"RAI","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.7519288"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have shown significant potential for domain-specific Question Answering (QA) tasks, although persistent challenges in retrieval precision and context selection continue to hinder their effectiveness. This study introduces Document Graph RAG (GraphRAG), a novel framework that bolsters retrieval robustness and enhances answer generation by incorporating Knowledge Graphs (KGs) built upon a document\u2019s intrinsic structure into the RAG pipeline. Through the application of the Design Science Research methodology, we systematically design, implement, and evaluate GraphRAG, leveraging graph-based document structuring and a keyword-based semantic linking mechanism to improve retrieval quality. The evaluation, conducted on well-established datasets including SQuAD, HotpotQA, and a newly developed manufacturing dataset, demonstrates consistent performance gains over a naive RAG baseline across both retrieval and generation metrics. The results indicate that GraphRAG improves Context Relevance metrics, with task-dependent optimizations for chunk size, keyword density, and top-k retrieval further enhancing performance. Notably, multi-hop questions benefit most from GraphRAG\u2019s structured retrieval strategy, highlighting its advantages in complex reasoning The purpose of the study is to analyze a RAG architecture and compare its retrieval quality with previously reported results for earlier retrieval-based QA approaches. Methodologically, the study first reviews earlier retrieval-based QA approaches used in the construction field. A RAG-based prototype was then implemented and evaluated on 86 construction-related questions. Retrieval quality was measured with Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), while answer correctness was evaluated manually using answer accuracy. The system combines vector-based passage retrieval with answer generation by a GPT model. The findings show that the prototype achieved an MRR of 0.65 for passage retrieval, which is slightly higher than previously reported values of about 0.55 for earlier retrieval-based QA in the same domain. The answer accuracy was 0.79. These results indicate that even a simple RAG architecture can provide useful answers in a specialized domain. The originality of the study lies in a methodological comparison between RAG-based and earlier retrieval-based QA results in the construction domain. In practical terms, the results highlight the value of RAG for professional information systems and digital libraries by enabling users to obtain direct answers instead of full documents. At the same time, expert verification remains important because generated answers may include unsupported
